title: Vertical ABM Pilot (Regulated Workloads) — Metrics Dashboard Spec (v0.9)
content:
Purpose
Track the 6–8 week Vertical ABM pilot (Regulated Workloads: FinServ + Healthcare) with a single source-of-truth spreadsheet that:
1) shows target coverage + outreach activity, 2) ties activity to pipeline outcomes (meetings → SQLs → POCs), 3) highlights bottlenecks (security reviews, evidence pack turnaround), and 4) captures qualitative signals that don’t fit cleanly in HubSpot.

Scope
- Accounts in the official target list only (see: target-account-list-finserv-health-sheet)
- Motions included: outbound email + LinkedIn, partner/co-sell intros, inbound from regulated landing page, webinar attendees
- Deal types: Redwood Dedicated + Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem)

Cadence + owners
- Daily updates (automated where possible): activity counts, meetings, stage, pipeline $ (Owner: Isabelle Laurent)
- Weekly manual update (Mon EOD): qualitative signals + security review status (Owner: AE on account + SDR)
- Weekly dashboard review (Thu ABM standup): summary tab + issues tab (Owner: Ben Carter)

Data sources (canonical)
- HubSpot: accounts/companies + deals + activities (meetings logged), lifecycle stages, pipeline, next step
- Gmail: outbound sends/replies (via sequences + manual labels) and “positive reply” flags
- LinkedIn: ad spend + clicks + form fills (only for the pilot campaign UTMs)
- Website analytics: regulated landing page views + conversions (UTM-based)
- Fireflies: call occurrence verification (fallback if meeting not logged)

Key definitions (do not improvise)
- Target account = appears on the pilot target list AND tagged in HubSpot with ABM Pilot = Regulated-2025
- Meeting booked = calendar meeting held or confirmed for a specific date with at least one target persona (Security/CISO, Platform/ML Eng, Procurement). Must be logged in HubSpot as a Meeting activity with outcome.
- Qualified meeting (QM) = meeting held AND at least one of: (a) dedicated/private deployment requirement, (b) security/compliance driver identified, (c) active project in next 6 months.
- SQL created = deal created in HubSpot AND moved to stage “SQL / Discovery” with MEDDICC fields minimally populated: pain, champion/decision-maker identified, timeline.
- Security review started = prospect requested evidence pack items OR completed security questionnaire kickoff OR scheduled a security review call.
- POC started = written POC plan agreed + start date set + Redwood SE assigned + at least one technical integration step completed (API key issued for Dedicated/Hosted trial OR Private/VPC deployment prerequisites shared).
- POC success = success criteria met + next-step agreed toward commercial (pilot expansion, procurement, or implementation plan).

Sheet structure (tabs)
TAB 0 — Readme & Change log
TAB 1 — Account coverage (target list + ownership)
TAB 2 — Activity & engagement (weekly rollups)
TAB 3 — Pipeline funnel (meetings → SQL → POC)
TAB 4 — Stage velocity (time in stage + bottlenecks)
TAB 5 — Security review tracker (evidence + questionnaire + blockers)
TAB 6 — Attribution & UTMs (webinar, ads, landing page)
TAB 7 — Qualitative signals (free text + scored signals)
TAB 8 — Data quality checks (missing fields, mismatches)

TAB 1 — Account coverage (target list + ownership)
Columns
- Account Name (text)
- Vertical (FinServ | Healthcare)
- Segment (Mid-market | Enterprise | Strategic)
- Region (NA | EMEA)
- Account Owner (AE) (Avery Johnson | Priyom Das | Hannah Schmitt | Diego Fernandez)
- SDR Owner (Grace O'Connor program; rep name as assigned)
- ABM Tier (1|2|3) (Tier 1 = 1:1, Tier 2 = 1:few, Tier 3 = scaled)
- Primary personas targeted (CISO/Security; Platform/ML Eng; Procurement)
- Known constraints (VPC required, on-prem required, residency, retention)
- HubSpot Company ID
- ABM Pilot Tag present? (Y/N)
- “Coverage status” (Not started | In sequence | Engaged | Meeting set | In pipeline)

Coverage metrics
- Target accounts total = COUNT(Account Name)
- Coverage = % with assigned AE AND SDR AND ABM Pilot Tag present
- Persona coverage = % with at least 1 named contact for each persona category

Owners
- Ownership fields: Sales Ops / Isabelle Laurent (with Sales leaders)
- Persona/contact completeness: SDR owner

TAB 2 — Activity & engagement (weekly rollups)
Goal: quick view of “are we running the motion?” and “are they responding?” without over-indexing on vanity metrics.

Columns (per account per week)
- Week starting (YYYY-MM-DD)
- Emails sent (count) — from HubSpot sequences + manual sends tracked by Gmail label “ABM-Regulated-2025”
- Emails delivered (count) — if available; else leave blank
- Positive replies (count) — definition: explicit interest, forward to correct owner, or asks for security info / meeting
- Neutral replies (count) — definition: “not now”, “check back”, “we have vendor”, but not unsubscribe
- Unsubscribes (count)
- LinkedIn touches (count) — connection requests + InMail + comments; manual entry OK
- Meetings set (count)
- Meetings held (count)
- Security review requests (count)

Engagement scoring (weekly)
- Engagement score (0–5)
  0 = no response + no signals
  1 = opens/clicks only OR website visit (low confidence)
  2 = neutral reply OR referral to another person
  3 = positive reply OR security FAQ request
  4 = meeting held + clear pain confirmed
  5 = active eval motion (POC plan, security review underway)

Data sources
- HubSpot sequence analytics (primary)
- Gmail label counts (fallback)
- LinkedIn manual entry (until we automate)

Owners
- SDR owner updates activity weekly; Isabelle/Tyler reconcile totals and remove duplicates.

TAB 3 — Pipeline funnel (meetings → SQL → POC)
This is the “executive-ready” funnel view.

Funnel stages (pilot-specific)
1) Targeted (in list)
2) Engaged (Engagement score ≥ 3)
3) Qualified meeting (QM)
4) SQL created
5) Security review started
6) POC started
7) POC success / Proposed (commercial next step)
8) Closed won

Columns
- Account Name
- Current funnel stage (picklist)
- Date entered stage (date)
- Date exited stage (date)
- Deal ID (HubSpot)
- Deal stage (HubSpot)
- Primary product motion (Dedicated | Private | TBD)
- Est. ARR / commit (text, use HubSpot amount if present)
- Primary blocker (Security bandwidth | Evidence pack | Residency | SSO/SAML | Procurement | Price | Competing build | Other)
- Next step date

Rollup metrics (top of tab)
- Total targeted accounts
- Engaged accounts
- QM count + rate (QM / targeted)
- SQL count + rate (SQL / QM)
- POC starts + rate (POC / SQL)
- Pipeline created $ (sum amounts for SQL+)
- Pipeline influenced $ (if we can confidently tie to ABM; see TAB 6 rules)

Success criteria (initial targets; revise after Week 2 baseline)
- Meetings held: 12–18 (combined)
- SQLs created: 6–10
- Security reviews started: 5–8
- POCs started: 2–4
- At least 1 deal in procurement by end of pilot (stretch)

Owners
- Ben Carter owns weekly readout; AEs own deal hygiene; Isabelle validates stage mapping.

TAB 4 — Stage velocity (time-in-stage + bottlenecks)
Purpose: identify where regulated deals stall (typically security review turnaround and deployment constraints).

Columns (deal-level)
- Deal Name
- Account Name
- Vertical
- Product motion (Dedicated | Private)
- Stage (HubSpot)
- Stage entered date
- Days in stage (calculated)
- “Regulated gate” status (None | Security review | DPA | Residency | Audit logging | SSO/SAML)
- Notes (1–2 lines)

Calculated metrics
- Median days from QM → SQL
- Median days from SQL → Security review started
- Median days from Security review started → POC started
- Median days from POC started → Proposed
- Stalled deals = Days in stage > threshold
  - Discovery/SQL: >14 days with no next step
  - Security review: >10 business days with open evidence requests
  - POC: >21 days without a checkpoint

Owners
- Isabelle Laurent maintains thresholds + weekly export
- Security team (Olga Petrov / Daniel Carter) uses this tab to prioritize responses when overloaded

TAB 5 — Security review tracker (evidence + questionnaire + blockers)
This is the operational tracker that prevents deals from dying during security.

Columns (account-level)
- Account Name
- Security contact name/title
- Security review call date (if scheduled)
- Security questionnaire received? (Y/N)
- Questionnaire owner (Olga Petrov | Naomi Feldman | other)
- Due date promised to prospect
- Evidence pack requested (list)
- Evidence pack items shared date
- SOC2 request (Y/N)
- Audit logs questions (Y/N; short note)
- KMS/HSM questions (Y/N; short note)
- SSO/SAML/SCIM questions (Y/N; short note)
- Data retention/residency questions (Y/N; short note)
- Open items (free text)
- Status (Not started | In progress | Blocked | Complete)

SLA targets (internal)
- First response to security request: < 1 business day (ack + owner assigned)
- Evidence pack index shared: < 2 business days (or explain constraints)
- Questionnaire turnaround: 5–10 business days depending on length (set expectation explicitly)

Owners
- Security tracker owner: Daniel Carter
- AE responsible for keeping due date accurate (don’t promise without confirming bandwidth)

TAB 6 — Attribution & UTMs (webinar, ads, landing page)
Purpose: keep attribution rules simple and auditable.

Standard UTM conventions (pilot)
- utm_campaign = abm_regulated_2025
- utm_source = linkedin | email | partner | webinar | organic
- utm_medium = paid_social | outbound | referral | event | organic
- utm_content = finserv_variant_a | finserv_variant_b | healthcare_variant_a | etc.
- utm_term = persona_jobtitle (optional; use only for paid)

Attribution rules (for pilot reporting)
- Pipeline “created” = deal created after the first ABM touch (email/linkedin/partner intro) within 45 days AND account is in target list.
- Pipeline “influenced” = deal existed prior, but had a pilot touchpoint within last 30 days AND progressed at least one stage during pilot window.
- If unclear, mark as “Unattributed (manual review)” and discuss in weekly standup.

Columns
- Contact email
- Account
- First touch date
- First touch source (picklist)
- First UTM captured (raw)
- Form fills (count)
- Webinar attended? (Y/N)
- Meeting booked within 14 days? (Y/N)
- Notes

Owners
- Tyler Benson owns UTMs + reporting consistency

TAB 7 — Qualitative signals (free text + scored)
Goal: capture regulated-specific buying signals that are leading indicators.

Columns (account-level; update weekly)
- Account Name
- Champion identified? (Y/N; name)
- Exec sponsor identified? (Y/N; name)
- Primary use case (fraud ops, member support, clinical summarization, coding assistance, platform inference standardization, etc.)
- “Regulated intensity” score (1–5)
  1 = standard SaaS security
  3 = SOC2 + SSO + retention
  5 = residency + audit export + on-prem/VPC hard requirement + procurement
- Competitive situation (Build | Existing vendor | Multiple | Unknown)
- Top 3 objections (free text)
- What resonated (latency/cost, deployment flexibility, auditability, operational tooling)
- Next step + risk (free text)

Owners
- AE owns narrative fields; SE adds technical notes when POC scoped

TAB 8 — Data quality checks
Common issues + how to fix
1) Meeting happened but not logged in HubSpot → AE/SDR must log Meeting activity and associate to company + deal
2) Account missing ABM Pilot tag → Isabelle to batch-fix weekly
3) Deal created but not linked to company/contact → fix associations; otherwise it will be missing from rollups
4) Duplicate companies (e.g., “Inc.” vs no suffix) → Sales Ops merges in HubSpot (flag in this tab)
5) Security review status drifting from reality → Daniel updates tracker, AE confirms in weekly

Checks (suggested formulas; implement in-sheet)
- Missing HubSpot Company ID = COUNTIF(blank)
- Missing owner (AE/SDR) = COUNTIF(blank)
- Meetings held (Fireflies exists) but HubSpot meeting count = 0 → manual reconciliation list
- Deals in SQL+ but MEDDICC fields blank → list + assign to AE

Notes / open questions
- LinkedIn activity is currently manual. If it becomes too noisy, we’ll only track “meaningful touches” (InMail sent, reply received) instead of every view/connection.
- For “positive replies,” we need consistent labeling (Gmail label or HubSpot outcome). Grace/Rohan to align SDR workflow by Week 2.
- For pipeline $, we will report both “net new pipeline created” and “pipeline in late stages” to avoid over-counting influenced deals.

Change log
- 2025-05-01: v0.1 initial tab plan + definitions (Tyler)
- 2025-05-08: added Security tracker SLA targets + regulated gate statuses (Isabelle + Daniel)
- 2025-05-16: clarified SQL + POC definitions; added attribution rules (Ben + Tyler)
- 2025-05-29: updated success criteria ranges after Week 2 baseline; added stalled thresholds (Isabelle)
